prompt:
Add a `tasklist` extension: a list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space becomes a task.
- The marker is replaced by `<input type="checkbox">`, `checked` for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` unless the `clickable` option is true (default false).
- The `<li>` gets the class from the `item_class` option (default `task`).
- It works in ordered and unordered lists, nested lists and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker.
Register it so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works once installed.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
I added the `tasklist` extension, and `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` now loads it. The full test suite passes (1142 tests, 112 skipped). flake8 isn't installed, so I only checked line lengths by hand. - **What it does:** a list item starting with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` and a space gets a checkbox in place of the marker. `[x]`/`[X]` add `checked`, `disabled` is added unless `clickable=True`, and the `
  • ` gets the `item_class` class (default `task`; an empty string adds no class). - **Where it works:** ordered, unordered, nested and loose lists (in a loose list the checkbox goes inside the `

    `). Inline markup after the marker is kept. - **Not converted:** a marker with no space after it, an escaped marker (`\[x]`), or one in the middle of the text. - **Design choice:** the conversion runs before inline parsing, so a `[x]` marker is never turned into a link when a `[x]: url` reference is defined. - **Registration:** the entry point is in both `pyproject.toml` and the fixture's `entry_points.txt`. I also added a docs page, an API reference page, the mkdocs nav entries, a row in the extensions index, and an `[unreleased]` changelog entry under "Added". The entry has no issue number (`#123`) because there isn't one. - **Not committed:** nothing is committed yet. Before you submit this upstream: the project docs say no new extensions will be added to Python-Markdown and new ones should be third-party packages. `docs/contributing.md` also requires a disclosure of AI use on contributions. Maintainers may turn it down on policy grounds.
